question: templetwo.com is not registered (Verisign whois returns NXDOMAIN). Cloudflare zone exists but is in 'pending' state awaiting nameserver propagation from a registrar. The Cloudflare tunnel works independently of DNS. Should the domain be registered? Through which registrar? Or is local-first sufficient and the domain unnecessary?
resolution: templetwo.com registered via Hostinger, DNS on Cloudflare (bart/michelle NS), stack.templetwo.com CNAME to tunnel. Permanent SSE endpoint live.

question: Jetson Orin Nano Super local RAG over .sovereign chronicle: does the proposed stack hold up? Working design as of May 25 2026: rsync-pull from HQ (one-way, --delete), embed with EmbeddingGemma-300M, store in Chroma, query with Gemma 4 E4B via Ollama. Open sub-questions: Does this work end-to-end as a local RAG against the chronicle?
resolution: YES — verified end-to-end 2026-05-26. Local RAG over the Jetson mirror works: embeddinggemma:300m -> Chroma (9071 chunks / 790 experiential files) -> gemma3:4b, all on the Orin GPU, fully offline. CLI at ~/sovereign-rag/chronicle_rag.py. Two qualifications baked into the design: (1) gen model is gemma3:4b, NOT the handoff Gemma 4 E4B — the gemma4 E-series OOM-kills on the 8GB Orin (e4b 9.6GB / e2b 7.2GB both exceed 7.4GiB shared RAM); (2) retrieval-first is the interface default — chunks are authority, generation is opt-in (--llm) and labeled orientation-only because the 4B can invert subtle lineage/relational frames (proven on a Mythos query). Sub-questions 2-5 (second reachable seat / sync cadence in practice / metadata-first vs pure semantic / expose as stack tool) remain open under sibling thread IDs.

Jetson Orin Nano Super local RAG over .sovereign chronicle: does the proposed stack hold up? Working design as of May 25 2026: rsync-pull from HQ (one-way, --delete), embed with EmbeddingGemma-300M, store in Chroma, query with Gemma 4 E4B via Ollama. Open sub-questions: Does the chronicle's structured metadata (tags, layer, intensity, timestamp) make tag-first / metadata-first retrieval better than pure semantic for most queries?
resolution: RESOLVED (hypothesis-strong): Yes, metadata-aware retrieval beats pure semantic, but as a TARGETED lever, not a blanket win. Built sovereign_chronicle_meta (8982 chunks, domain/layer/intensity/timestamp as queryable Chroma metadata) and a hybrid rerank (0.72 cosine + 0.18 tag-overlap + 0.05 intensity + 0.05 recency, pool 40). Stable across 5 runs: on the Mythos lineage query semantic never surfaces the framing-correction insight in top-10; hybrid puts it at #1 every run. Ties semantic on exact-fact technical queries. tag=0.18 keeps the win without demoting exact matches (0.25 was too hot). SHIPPED: chronicle_rag.py defaults to hybrid + --semantic-only escape hatch. Caveat: n=6, self-authored eval, so hypothesis-strong not ground_truth; the Mythos miss-to-#1 is robust, the ties softer. Generalizable keeper: metadata wins where curation front-loaded meaning into tags (relational/lineage material), neutral where the answer is a literal string. Full detail in insight jetson-local-rag,sub-question-4,metadata-retrieval,hybrid,resolved. Sub-questions 2 (redundant seat), 3 (sync cadence — note: cron pull PAUSED 2026-05-26 per Anthony, mirror frozen for clean experiment), 5 (Jetson as peer stack tool) remain open.
